tierWindow.goal: Put reflection to work: use a structured cycle to work through an experience, push past describing it to reflecting on it critically, and turn that reflection into a concrete action for next time.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application (apply, use, distinguish, produce, plan) on the learner's own recent academic experiences.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: A whole cycle held together at once; applying a named model to an experience rather than only recognising that reflection matters.
tierWindow.autonomy: Moderate scaffolding; worked examples that model the cycle, then guided application the learner performs; feedback explains the reasoning.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner has met reflection at the introductory tier: they know what reflection is and why it matters for learning at university. This course assumes that grounding and turns it into a structured practice the learner performs - using a cycle, reflecting critically rather than only describing, and acting on what they find. It does not yet treat reflection as an ongoing professional practice, which is the advanced tier's concern.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, reflecting with a structure: using a cycle so you work through an experience in set stages rather than at random. Second, from describing to reflecting: pushing past what happened to why it happened and what it means. Third, turning reflection into action: closing the loop so a reflection produces something you will actually do. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about putting reflection to work. You already know what reflection is and why it matters; now you will turn it into a practice you can actually carry out. By the end you will be able to use a structured reflective cycle to work through an experience, reflect critically on it rather than only describing it, and turn that reflection into a concrete action for next time.

Reflection is one of the habits that separates a self-regulating learner from a passive one. Done well, it is how you learn from what you do, not just how much you do.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: use a structured reflective cycle, reflect critically rather than only describing, and turn a reflection into a concrete action.

practiceConnection.academic: Reflection is built into how academic and professional work improves. Every placement log, every portfolio, every time a tutor asks what you would do differently, draws on the same practice. Learning to reflect with structure, depth and a clear action now means each experience in your studies becomes something you genuinely learn from, and the habit carries directly into professional life.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced reflective practice course takes these habits into reflection as a professional practice, sustained, evidenced, and part of how you develop as a graduate. Going wider: the same cycle underpins Work-Based and Experiential Learning, Presenting, and Understanding Learning, Assessment and Feedback, where you put structured reflection to work on real tasks.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Reflection is no longer just something you know you should do: it is a practice you can carry out. You can use a structured cycle to work through an experience in set stages, rather than reflecting at random. You can push past describing what happened to reflecting critically on why it happened and what your part was. And you can turn that reflection into a concrete action that changes your next attempt. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, reflection is something you practise across your degree and beyond. Every placement, portfolio, group project and piece of feedback is a chance to run the cycle: work through the experience, reflect on it with real depth, and act on what you find. It is also what professional life expects, and learning to reflect deliberately now is what the advanced tier of this pathway develops into a full professional practice.
